subject: Post-call: pinning priority matrix and recovery expectations
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@medibridge.health>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@medibridge.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up & clarifications from today's residency discussion

Hi Asha / Rajiv — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap below and a few clarifying asks so we can scope an accurate config and cost estimate.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary requirement: keep patient-identifiable data serving and storage within EU EEA.
- Acceptable failover model: warm standby in US for DR with data encrypted and access audited; cross-border processing only when triggered by failover events.
- Retention: two classes — PII (30 days hot, 90 days cold archive) and non-PII telemetry (180 days).
- Logging: audit logs must be exportable and immutable for 1 year; tokenized identifiers preferred.

Questions we still need from you
1) Are there any contractual restrictions that prevent us from storing encrypted backups in the US, even if keys remain in your KMS in the EU?
2) For failover events, what RTO / RPO are you targeting (e.g., RTO <= 2 hours, RPO <= 15 mins)?
3) Any specific key management provider (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, or customer HSM) preference?
4) Do you require per-tenant key rotation audits surfaced in the console or monthly delivered reports?

Proposed next steps from Redwood (we can adjust once you confirm answers)
- We will draft a pin-priority matrix that maps environments + datasets to region pins and warm-standby behavior (attached draft).
- Security team will send a short questionnaire focused on encryption, key ownership, and audit export formats (cc: security@medibridge.health).
- If the matrix looks good, propose a technical walkthrough (30–45m) the week of Dec 14 to validate network flows and KMS integration.

Attachments included: redwood-pin-priority-matrix.pdf (draft), questionnaire stub (we'll finalize once you confirm KMS preference).

Resources: I also added a short Drive folder with our failover diagrams and a sample SOC 2 intake pack.

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0129
[Attachment: redwood-pin-priority-matrix.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@medibridge.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@medibridge.health>, security@medibridge.health, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:41:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up & clarifications from today's residency discussion

Thanks Michael — good summary. Asha is OOO today; I can answer a few items and then she'll confirm the legal bits next week.

Answers:
- Backups: we are OK with encrypted backups stored in the US if encryption keys never leave the EU. We need proof-of-concept of key separation (customer-managed keys preferred).
- RTO/RPO: target RTO <= 2 hours and RPO <= 30 minutes for production traffic. Non-critical environments can be longer.
- KMS: preferred is Azure Key Vault, but we are open to AWS KMS if we can bring our own keys. HSM is a must for any long-term archival access.
- Audit reports: monthly delivered reports + immediate alerts for any key rotation or key usage anomalies.

Requests from our side:
- Can you confirm whether cross-region reads for inference are strictly blocked unless a failover is initiated? We need assurance that normal ops won't accidentally route EU traffic through US nodes.
- We will attach the initial security questionnaire later today from security@medibridge.health.

Quick note: we'll need a short write-up for procurement describing the warm-standby cost delta vs. fully geo-redundant (just a paragraph).

Regards,
Rajiv
Head of Platform Ops | MediBridge Health
rajiv.m@medibridge.health
[Attachment: medibridge-data-questionnaire.xlsx (XLSX, 7 questions)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@medibridge.health>, Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@medibridge.health>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, security@medibridge.health
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up & clarifications from today's residency discussion

Rajiv — thanks for the quick responses. Quick answers inline below and an ask for the procurement blurb (we can draft).

> Can you confirm whether cross-region reads for inference are strictly blocked unless a failover is initiated?
Short answer: yes — under the pinning policy we propose, production traffic bound to an EU pin will be routed only to EU-serving nodes. Cross-region reads are only permitted during an active failover policy you approve. We'll document the trigger and approval flow.

> KMS / key separation
We support customer-managed keys in both Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS. For HSM-backed keys we can integrate with your HSM via a networked gateway; for archive keys we recommend key wrapping where the master KEK remains in your vault.

Proposed recovery plan summary (for procurement blurb) — draft you can copy: 
"Warm-standby configuration keeps active primary serving in the EU with synchronized, encrypted snapshots to a US cold-warm pool. In failover, traffic is redirected to the warm pool within the agreed RTO with replayable state to meet RPO objectives. Warm-standby reduces overall cost vs. fully geo-active by keeping US capacity warm (pre-warmed GPUs and pre-loaded models) rather than fully active. Estimated delta: ~40–60% of fully geo-active, depending on throughput and model size."

Next steps
- Ben / Security will review the attached questionnaire and respond by EOD tomorrow with the compliance artifacts (SOC 2 summary, encryption whitepaper).
- Michael will schedule the technical walkthrough once Asha confirms timing.

I've attached an updated pin-priority matrix with a proposed EU-first pin -> US warm-standby mapping. Please let us know if you want the matrix as a table or an annotated diagram.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-pin-priority-matrix.pdf (PDF, updated)]

From: Asha Pillai <asha.pillai@medibridge.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@medibridge.health>, security@medibridge.health
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up & clarifications from today's residency discussion

Thanks all — this looks good. Asha here (back from travel) — confirming:
- EU-first pin with US warm-standby is acceptable provided the key separation is demonstrable and we have the audit export for key usage.
- RTO/RPO targets above are fine. We'll add a 30-day cutover test window requirement in the contract (we'll propose language).
- Please share the SOC 2 summary and the encryption integration diagram before the walkthrough.

Action items for Redwood
- Share SOC 2 summary + whitepaper (Ben).
- Share a short demo script for the walkthrough and one-week availability for Dec 14–20 (Michael).
- Include the procurement blurb in a one-page costs appendix (Ben/Michael).

I'll loop procurement once we have the cost appendix. Looking forward to the walkthrough.

Best,
Asha Pillai
VP, Platform | MediBridge Health
asha.pillai@medibridge.health
[Inline: forwarded medibridge questionnaire to security@redwood.com]
